problems.title: A square plus its root
problems.question: Natural a, b, c satisfy b=√a, c=a+b. Which of 25,30,100,303 can c be?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
steps: At b=5, c=25+5=30. The other candidates fall strictly between consecutive products:20<25<30,90<100<110,272<303<306.

problems.title: A two-variable system
problems.question: How many ordered pairs satisfy x+y=1, xy=0?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: $xy=0$ means x=0 or y=0.
steps: These give (0,1) and (1,0), both valid and distinct.

problems.title: Cancel opposite radicals
problems.question: Evaluate $(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)^2+\sqrt{24}$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: $(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)^2=5-2\sqrt6$, and $\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6$.
steps: The radical terms cancel.

problems.title: Integer solutions of an absolute inequality
problems.question: How many integers satisfy $|x^2-2x-3|<3x+3$?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: An inequality $|u|<v$ is equivalent to $-v<u<v$.
steps: The upper bound gives x²−5x−6<0, or −1<x<6. The lower gives x²+x>0, or x<−1 or x>0. Their intersection is 0<x<6. The integers are 1,2,3,4,5.

problems.title: Rectangle standing on a diameter
problems.question: A rectangle has one side of length 12 on a circle diameter, and its opposite vertices on the circle. Its other side is 8. Find the radius.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The centre lies under the rectangle’s horizontal midpoint. A radius to a top vertex has legs 12/2 and 8.

problems.title: Leg projections on a hypotenuse
problems.question: A right-angle bisector divides the hypotenuse in ratio 3:2. Find the ratio of the leg projections on the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The angle-bisector theorem gives leg ratio 3:2. The projection theorem gives projections $a^2/c, b^2/c$.
steps: Their ratio is the squared leg ratio.

problems.title: Three simultaneous claims
problems.question: Find a making all true: (2a−6)x=5 is solvable; √a is real; y=(a²−36)x+8 passes through (1,8).
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The conditions are $a\ne3$, $a\ge0$, and $a^2=36$.
steps: The third gives ±6; the nonnegative restriction leaves 6, which also meets a≠3.

problems.title: Two half-angles
problems.question: Same-side interior angle bisectors between parallels make acute angles α,β with the parallels. Their difference is 20°. Find the smaller.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The original angles sum to 180°, so $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$.
steps: Together with |α−β|=20°, the smaller is (90−20)/2.

problems.title: Parallelogram vertex coordinates
problems.question: OABC is a parallelogram with O=(0,0), A=(1,3), C=(4,0). Find B.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: $B=A+C-O$.
steps: Add coordinates (1+4,3+0).

problems.title: Strict polynomial inequality
problems.question: Solve $(3x-5)^2(x-7)<0$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The square is positive except at x=5/3, where the product is 0.
steps: Thus require x<7 and exclude x=5/3.

problems.title: A point on a reciprocal graph
problems.question: (3a, a) lies on y=12/x. Find the sum of all a.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
steps: The two values are −2 and 2.

problems.title: Chord midpoint on a diameter
problems.question: A diameter CD passes through midpoint F of chord AB. AB=10, CF=12. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The diameter through a chord midpoint is perpendicular to that chord, so $AF=5$ and $\angle AFC=90^\circ$.

problems.title: Absolute value equals its negative
problems.question: Solve $|(x+2)(x-5)|=-x^2+3x+10$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The right side is $-(x+2)(x-5)$. The identity $|u|=-u$ holds exactly for $u\le0$.
steps: Thus (x+2)(x−5)≤0, giving the closed interval between the roots.

problems.title: A quartic with no real roots
problems.question: Find all a for which $x^4+2(a+1)x^2+4a=0$ has no real solution.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Put $t=x^2\ge0$. The equation is $t^2+2(a+1)t+4a=0$.
steps: For a>0 all terms are positive for t≥0, so no root exists. At a=0, t=0 is a root. For a<0, the polynomial is negative at t=0 and tends to +∞, so it has a positive root.

problems.title: Incentre divides a bisector
problems.question: In ABC, BC=a, AC=b, AB=c. Bisector BD meets AC at D; O is the incentre. Find OD:OB.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The incentre is $O=(aA+bB+cC)/(a+b+c)$, while $D=(aA+cC)/(a+c)$.
steps: Therefore O=[(a+c)D+bB]/(a+b+c), giving OD/OB=b/(a+c).

problems.title: Bases from a midpoint segment
problems.question: A trapezoid has angles 33°,57° at its larger base, midline 8 and distance 4 between base midpoints. Find the bases.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Let the horizontal offsets of the two legs be u, v and height h. Since the angles sum to 90°, $uv=h^2$.
steps: The midpoint segment squared is h²+(u−v)²/4=(u+v)²/4. Thus the base difference u+v is 8. The base sum is twice the midline,16. Solve the sum and difference.

problems.title: Rational inequality
problems.question: Solve $2+8/x<0$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
steps: The numerator and denominator have opposite signs precisely between −4 and 0.

problems.title: A composed linear function
problems.question: f(x)=4x−5 and (m,4) is on y=f(2x). Find m.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
steps: Set 4=8m−5, giving 8m=9.

problems.title: Diagonals in two cyclic trapezoids
problems.question: Two trapezoids inscribed in the same circle have corresponding sides parallel. Find the ratio of corresponding diagonals.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: A chord diagonal subtending an angle θ has length $2R\sin\theta$.
steps: Corresponding vertex angles are equal or supplementary because their side lines are parallel; they therefore have the same sine. Both circumradii are R. Thus the corresponding diagonals have equal lengths.

problems.title: Gcd and lcm
problems.question: Natural m, n have gcd q>1. Find their lcm.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: $\gcd(m, n)\operatorname{lcm}(m, n)=mn$.
steps: Divide mn by q.

problems.title: Centroid in a right triangle
problems.question: ABC is right-angled at C and centroid G satisfies CG=6. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The centroid takes $2/3$ of the median from the vertex; the median to a right triangle’s hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse.
steps: Thus CG=(2/3)(AB/2)=AB/3.

problems.title: Exactly two triangle properties
problems.question: Exactly two statements are true: ABC is right-angled; ABC is isosceles; ABC has a 45° angle. Find its angles.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: A right triangle with a 45° angle must be 45°–45°–90°, making all three statements true. A right isosceles triangle does the same.
steps: Thus the right-angle statement is false, and the other two true. If 45° were a base angle, the triangle would be right; therefore 45° is the apex and the equal angles are (180−45)/2.

problems.title: Parabola roots from axis and intercept
problems.question: y=x²+bx+c has y-intercept 12 and symmetry axis x=4. Find its x-intercepts.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
steps: Factor x²−8x+12=(x−2)(x−6).

problems.title: Zeros of a radical product
problems.question: How many roots has $\sqrt[3]{x^2-5x+4}\sqrt{-x^2+5x-6}=0$?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The square-root domain is $[2,3]$. The cube-root factor vanishes at 1 and 4.
steps: Those two values are outside the domain. The square-root factor vanishes at both endpoints 2 and 3.

problems.title: Circle radius from tangent and nearest distance
problems.question: An exterior point A is 2 cm from a circle’s nearest point and its tangent length is $2\sqrt6$. Find the radius.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: $AO=r+2$, and tangent power gives $AO^2-r^2=24$.
steps: Thus (r+2)²−r²=4r+4=24.

problems.title: A trapezoid with a bisecting diagonal
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 3,5. One diagonal is perpendicular to a leg, the other bisects an angle at the larger base. Find height.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Take A=(0,0), D=(5,0), B=(u, h), C=(u+3, h), with AC perpendicular to CD and BD bisecting angle D.
steps: The bisector and parallel bases give CD=BC=3. Put v=2−u, the horizontal projection of CD. Then h²+v²=9. Perpendicularity gives h²=(5−v)v. Subtract to get 9=5v, so v=9/5 and h²=9−81/25=144/25. The reflected configuration gives the same height.

problems.title: A median divides a cevian
problems.question: AM:MB=3:2 on AB. Median BK meets MC at O. Find MO:OC.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Take masses $m_A=2, m_B=3$, so $m_M=5$. Since K is midpoint of AC, take $m_C=2$.
steps: On MC the ratio MO/OC equals mC/mM.

problems.title: Exactly one product-equation root
problems.question: For which a does $(\sqrt x-1)(x-a)=0$ have exactly one solution?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Domain $x\ge0$. The fixed root is x=1; another root x=a exists only when a≥0.
steps: To avoid a second distinct root, either a<0 or a=1. At a=0 there are two roots,0 and 1.

problems.title: Axis intercepts of an absolute quotient
problems.question: Find axis intercepts of $y=(|1-x|+1)/(|x|+x)$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The denominator is nonzero only for x>0. The numerator is always at least 1.
steps: Thus x=0 is outside the domain, so there is no y-intercept. The function never equals 0, so there is no x-intercept.

problems.title: Minimum under a product constraint
problems.question: Minimise $x^2+y^2$ if $(x+4)(y-4)=0$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The condition means x=−4 or y=4.
steps: On x=−4, the sum is 16+y²≥16, attained at y=0. On y=4 it is x²+16≥16, attained at x=0.

problems.title: Bisector perpendicular to a median
problems.question: The B-bisector is perpendicular to the median to AB. AC=10 and perimeter ABC=31. Find BC.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Put B at the origin and its bisector on the x-axis. Write $A=(c\cos\theta, c\sin\theta)$ and $C=(a\cos\theta,-a\sin\theta)$.
steps: The median joins C to A/2. Perpendicularity to the x-axis gives a cosθ=(c/2)cosθ. Since θ is half a triangle angle, cosθ≠0, so c=2a. The perimeter gives a+c=21, hence a=7.

problems.title: Equivalent equations
problems.question: For which a do $x^2-a=0$ and $\sqrt x-a=0$ have the same real solution set?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: For a<0 both sets are empty. At a=0 both give {0}.
steps: For a>0 the first has two roots ±√a while the second has just the nonnegative root a², so they cannot be equivalent.

problems.title: An even combination
problems.question: For any real-defined f, what symmetry must f(x)+f(−x) have?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Let $g(x)=f(x)+f(-x)$. Then $g(-x)=f(-x)+f(x)=g(x)$.
steps: This is exactly the definition of an even function.

problems.title: An increasing quadratic on an interval
problems.question: For which a is y=x²−2ax+5 increasing on [−3,−2]?
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: $y\prime=2(x-a)$. Its smallest value on the interval is $2(-3-a)$.
steps: Require this to be nonnegative, giving a≤−3. Equality at the endpoint still gives a strictly increasing function on the interval.

problems.title: Maximum of a semicircle expression
problems.question: f(x)=$\sqrt{7-x^2+6x}$ has maximum b at x=a. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
steps: Its maximum radicand is 16 at a=3, so b=4.

problems.title: Circle through the incentre and two vertices
problems.question: A triangle has sides 1,2 with included angle 60°. A circle passes through the incentre and the endpoints of the third side. Find its radius.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The third side has length $a=\sqrt{1+4-4\cos60^\circ}=\sqrt3$. The incentre angle opposite it is $90^\circ+60^\circ/2=120^\circ$.
steps: In this new triangle the circumradius is a/(2sin120°)=√3/√3=1.
problems.note: None of the printed choices √7,√6,4,3 equals 1.

problems.title: A quadratic soluble for every linear coefficient
problems.question: Find q such that $x^2+px+q=0$ has at least one real root for every real p.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: The discriminant must satisfy $p^2-4q\ge0$ for every p. Its minimum in p is −4q at p=0.
steps: Thus q≤0 is necessary and sufficient.

problems.title: A system in square roots
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt x+\sqrt y=3$, x−y=3.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Let $u=\sqrt x, v=\sqrt y$, both nonnegative. Then $u+v=3$ and $(u-v)(u+v)=3$.
steps: Thus u−v=1. Solve to get u=2, v=1, then square.

problems.title: A cubic inequality on a radical domain
problems.question: Solve $(x\sqrt x)^2-3|-x|-4\le0$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Domain x≥0. There the inequality is $p(x)=x^3-3x-4\le0$.
steps: The derivative 3x²−3 is negative on [0,1) and positive on (1,∞). Since p(0)=−4, p(1)=−6, there is just one positive zero α. Cardano’s identity gives α=∛(2+√3)+∛(2−√3): the two cube roots have product 1, so α³=4+3α. The inequality holds from 0 through α.

problems.title: Integer solutions by factoring
problems.question: Find all integer solutions of $x^2-3xy-10y^2+19=0$.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Factor as $(x-5y)(x+2y)=-19$.
steps: The two factors are integers, so their ordered possibilities are (1,−19),(−1,19),(19,−1),(−19,1). Their difference, (x+2y)−(x−5y)=7y, would be ±20 in every case. Since 20 is not divisible by 7, none yields integer y.

problems.title: Circumradius after an incircle condition
problems.question: ABC is right at C, AC=6, BC=8. D lies on BC and triangle ACD has inradius 1. Find the circumradius of ADB.
problems.idea: Use the standard relation and verify all restrictions.
formulas: Put CD=t. In the right triangle ACD, $1=(6+t-\sqrt{36+t^2})/2$.
steps: This gives √(36+t²)=t+4, hence 36=8t+16 and t=5/2. Thus AD=13/2, BD=11/2, AB=10. Area ADB=(1/2)·BD·AC=33/2. Use R=AD·BD·AB/(4 are a).
